\ draw_column: the part's columns from col_ptr, ds_c of them, each from its bottom's cell
\ b_ptr raised by its first row. Y = the line in the character cell indexes the screen (s_ptr =
\ the cell), the data and the save block together; each cell has 8 bytes of the save block (the
\ lines it does not draw are left unused), so moving up a cell is the data 8 back, the save
\ block 8 on and the screen a character row (&280) up. Saves each screen byte, then writes
\ (byte AND mask) EOR pixel, as the plotter does with the player. Each column's record (count
\ - 1, the lowest byte's address) goes 8 bytes after the last cell before it (v_ptr + 8: v_ptr
\ is that cell's base), its cells after the record; restore_block walks them the same way.
.draw_column
{
    BRA each                        \ 65C02 opcode
.empty
    LDA col_ptr                     \ an empty column: 2 bytes
    CLC
    ADC #2
    STA col_ptr
    BCS empty_hi                    \ the page crossed (rare)
.to_next
    JMP next
.empty_hi
    INC col_ptr + 1
    BRA to_next                     \ 65C02 opcode

\ draw_column: the part's columns from col_ptr, ds_c of them, each from its bottom's cell
\ b_ptr raised by its first row. Y = the line in the character cell indexes the screen (s_ptr =
\ the cell), the data and the save block together; each cell has 8 bytes of the save block (the
\ lines it does not draw are left unused), so moving up a cell is the data 8 back, the save
\ block 8 on and the screen a character row (&280) up. Saves each screen byte, then writes
\ (byte AND mask) EOR pixel, as the plotter does with the player. Each column's record (count
\ - 1, the lowest byte's address) goes 8 bytes after the last cell before it (v_ptr + 8: v_ptr
\ is that cell's base), its cells after the record; restore_block walks them the same way.
.draw_column
{
    BRA each                        \ 65C02 opcode
.empty
    DEC ds_c                        \ an empty column: next_c's DEC ds_c : BEQ done, first. The last column returns
    BEQ ren_draw_sprite.drawn       \ here, before col_ptr is stepped on past it (dead once the sprite is drawn:
    LDA col_ptr                     \ ren_draw_sprite loads it afresh): 2 bytes on
    CLC
    ADC #2
    STA col_ptr
    BCS empty_hi                    \ the page crossed (rare)
.empty_join_f
    SEC
    JMP next_c + 4                  \ on into next_c at its BIT dm_flip (past its DEC ds_c : BEQ done), C = 1
.to_next
    JMP next
.empty_hi
    INC col_ptr + 1
    BRA empty_join_f                \ 65C02 opcode (C = 1 already: the SEC is redundant, not wrong)
candidates.summary: draw_column's empty column: DEC ds_c and BEQ to the RTS first, so the last column of a part (27% of empty columns, 1.16 a pass) returns before col_ptr is stepped on past it (col_ptr is dead then: 20 cycles saved); the others finish with SEC / JMP next_c + 4 (past next_c's DEC ds_c : BEQ done), which saves JMP next's BRA (3 cycles). The flipped carry path's high-byte step is INC b_ptr + 1 / BPL / LDA #&40 / STA (the LDA / INC A / STA was 3 cycles slower and a byte longer): 7 bytes larger overall, which is all the room the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW build has in bank 4 (7 bytes spare; the gate's 'full'). Measured on the bench build 2026-10-22 (scratch copy of HEAD ff62e12): work a pass 34457 -> 34425 (seed 1), 39690 -> 39651 (RIGHT). Alternative to the next candidate (same empty lines, overlaps it).
candidates.equivalence: Empty column (count 0, A = 0, Y = 1 on entry from each's BEQ empty). Old: col_ptr += 2 (page crossed: high byte +1), then JMP next = SEC / BRA next_c = DEC ds_c / BEQ done (RTS) / BIT dm_flip ... New: DEC ds_c / BEQ ren_draw_sprite.drawn (an RTS 33 bytes back; same stack, ds_c = 0) first; if ds_c is not 0 the same col_ptr step (BCS empty_hi: INC col_ptr + 1 then BRA to the SEC), then SEC / JMP next_c + 4, which is next_c's BIT dm_flip (DEC ds_c is 2 bytes, BEQ done 2): ds_c decremented once, C = 1, as the old reached it; A is the new low byte of col_ptr in both and Z/N are reset by BIT. On the last column the old stepped col_ptr (and col_ptr + 1) before returning, the new does not: &C7/&C8 differ on return. Nothing reads them: ren_draw_sprite stores col_ptr afresh before any use (lines 1589-1591), no other source mentions col_ptr, save_game_zp keeps only &B0-&BB and &C0 of that area, and registers and flags are dead at the RTS (draw_mover's caller reloads, sky's .kept stores fresh). to_next / JMP next is unchanged (have_j's BCC to_next). The flipped carry path: old LDA b_ptr + 1 / INC A / BPL / LDA #&40 / STA b_ptr + 1; new INC b_ptr + 1 / BPL (taken: the incremented value stays, the same one stored) / LDA #&40 / STA b_ptr + 1 (N set after the INC: the &80 wrap, the same &40 stored); A and flags are dead (next is draw_column's BRA each, then each: LDY #1 / LDA (col_ptr),Y), C = 1 either way (INC leaves it).
candidates.relies_on: (1) col_ptr (&C7/&C8) is dead when ren_draw_sprite returns (only render.6502 lines 50, 1589, 1591 and draw_column use it; render_zp keeps &B0-&BB and &C0 only). (2) next_c's first four bytes stay DEC ds_c (zp) and BEQ done: JMP next_c + 4 is an entry past a label (nothing else in src/ refers to next_c), so a candidate for the next_c lines must keep it. (3) .drawn (ren_draw_sprite) stays an RTS reached by this BEQ (backward, in range, same page &9B). (4) Room: the 'full' (DEBUG_FULLREDRAW) build has exactly 7 bytes spare in bank 4 and this takes 7 (assembled: bench, full, ship, release, gameplay, SKY_HELI=0 all build); any other candidate growing bank 4 in that build must wait. (5) Page crossings: everything after the window moves 7 bytes; measured whole-pass in the bench build, the one hot branch that newly crosses is BEQ no_part (&9DD0 -> &9DD7, +1.5 cycles a pass, inside the measured gain); the window's own taken branches stay in page &9B. Verified: passlock base vs this build, 2,500 passes seed 1 with --screen, state and screen identical.

candidates.old:
LDA ds_c                        \ flipped: the bottom 8 * (n - 1) on
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A

candidates.new:
LDA ds_c                         \ flipped: the bottom 8 * (n - 1) on
    DEC A                            \ 65C02 opcode
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A                            \ C = 0: n <= 12 (every sprite drawn, sprite_column_count), so n - 1 < 32
    ADC b_ptr
candidates.summary: The flipped start's 8 * (n - 1): drop the CLC after the three ASLs. n is a sprite's column count, at most 12 for every sprite that has a straight image (sprite_columns.6502: the one count over 31, &82 at sprite &32, has no image: straight_sprite_hi = 0, and ren_draw_sprite returns at its BNE known), so n - 1 < 32 and the third ASL leaves C = 0. 1 byte smaller; measured only -2 (seed 1), -1 (RIGHT) on the bench build: marginal.
candidates.equivalence: ds_c = n here (ren_draw_sprite stored it from sprite_column_count; compiled_part restores it from ds_n when it falls back). For 1 <= n <= 32, (n - 1) << 3 does not carry out of the byte, so C = 0 after the third ASL and ADC b_ptr adds exactly what CLC / ADC did, with the same carry out for the BCC after STA. For n = 0 (DEC A = &FF) C would be 1, but no sprite that reaches here has n = 0 (sprites &32 and &36 have no image).
candidates.relies_on: The generated column counts (src/sprite_columns.6502, 'the sprite data never changes') stay at 32 or fewer for every sprite with an image; if tools/sprites.py ever emitted a larger count this would break. Page crossings: everything after moves 1 byte down; measured whole-pass on the bench build (34455 / 39689), no new hot crossing.
